In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the SS model in the analysis of multiple indicator data from a non-homogeneous system can lead to significant and unpredictable errors in the estimates of VE and PS.

the SS model should only be used in situations where the capillary permeabilities of the red cells and plasma are equal and where the red cell and plasma volumes are negligible compared to the extravascular volume.
the SS model can be used to estimate capillarity permeability and extravascular volume only if it is assumed that red cells are impermeable and the plasma-to-red cell flow rate ratio is unity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
if the 4-phase SS model is to be used to describe the capillary-tissue system, then the model must accurately describe the c(t) curve.
the SS model is not appropriate for estimating capillary PS or VE when red cells are permeable to the indicator or when the red cells are not equilibrated with the indicator prior to injection.
if the tracer is not equilibrated with blood before injection and if the capillary permeability of erythrocytes is not known, then the plasma-tissue model should be used.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SS model is not a good choice for estimating capillary PS or VE from tracer concentration data obtained from a heterogeneous capillaries unit.
the SS model is not always appropriate for use when capillaries are heterogeneous in structure.
application of the whole blood or plasma-tissue SS models to multiple indicator data collected in the capillary bed can lead to erroneous estimates of capillar PS and VE.
